doc.title: Robert Glasper interviewed by Greg Thomas, Clinton, New York, February 20, 2016

chapter: Kendrick Lamar and To Pimp a Butterfly
title: Terrace Martin and early road work as a student
summary: He met Terrace Martin at a jazz camp, and went on the road with Christian McBride, Russell Malone and Terence Blanchard while at the New School.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Now tell us about your collaboration with Kendrick Lamar on “To Pimp a Butterfly.”

Yeah, Kendrick, first of all a lot of my friends are on that, are producers on that, on all the Kendrick stuff from “Section.80” and “good kid, m.A.A.d. city” and all his records. One in particular, Terrace Martin, a producer, I went to jazz camp with Terrace in high school, when I was 15 years old, and we met each other then. He’s in L.A. He’s from L.A. and we all met at Loyola in New Orleans, they had like a national high school jazz band thing. We were both in there. So we kept in touch all through the years. And he used to call me up to do Snoop Dogg tours and stuff, because he was Snoop Dog’s music director too. I was never around to do them. As soon as I got in college I pretty much went on the road with Christian McBride and Russell Malone and Terence and a few other people.
Terence Blanchard. So I was never really at school very much. Especially my sophomore year on I was gone a lot.
Okay. And it’s good to go to a school that —
That allows you to do that. Yeah. I still had to fight. Some of them teachers was wishing they was on the gig.
